properties.name: Lake Poopó (center)
properties.description: The former center of Lake Poopó, Bolivia's second-largest lake until its desiccation in 2015. Covering up to 3,000 km² at its peak.

properties.name: City of Oruro
properties.description: Departmental capital and nearest major city to Lake Poopó. The city declared the lake's disappearance in December 2015.

properties.name: Huanuni Tin Mine
properties.description: State-owned tin mine in the Cordillera Central, one of the largest mining operations in the region. Its water-intensive processes divert and contaminate Lake Poopó's feeder streams.

properties.name: Desaguadero River Source
properties.description: The Desaguadero River carries runoff from Lake Titicaca and has historically been Lake Poopó's primary water source.

properties.name: Lake Uru Uru
properties.description: A smaller lake north of Poopó, designated along with Poopó as a Ramsar Wetland of International Importance in 2002.

properties.name: Chipaya
properties.description: A large Uru community north of the Coipasa Salt Flat where the Pukina language continues strongly. Source of language teachers for the revival project.

properties.name: Azanaques Mountains
properties.description: Part of the Andean Cordillera Central bordering Lake Poopó to the east. The 'Bolivian Tin Belt' with 437 mining concessions registered around the lake.
